- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >1.5x recent mean), model often overshoots in next 3–7 days; apply decay factor (e.g., 0.8–0.9) to forecasted values.
- If sentiment turns positive (≥0.67) after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast by 10–20% for 1–3d horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >2.5x recent 18d average, cap at 1.5x average; if <0.5x, floor at 0.3x average.
- Sentiment spikes (≥0.67) in last 3–5 days correlate with underestimation; adjust forecast upward by 15–25% for 1–5d horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) and history shows low volatility; add 0.1–0.2 to forecast for 1–7d horizon.
